title: Governmental rationalities and misrecognising human and social conditions in English-in-education policy for individual and social development
core_idea: To interrogate how English-in-education policy, framed as a tool for individual and social development, relates to students and parents in low socioeconomic contexts by treating development as an ideology and applying social theories (Bourdieu, Foucault, Sara Ahmed); the study focuses on a single school in Bangladesh and gathers perspectives from the principal, English teachers, parents, and students through interviews and focus groups analyzed thematically.
tldr: A qualitative, theory-informed examination of how development-framed English-in-education policy is experienced by low-SES students and parents in a Bangladeshi school, aiming to critique assumptions in language policy and its implications for equitable language education.
